title: Noon Chai with Girda
description: Traditional Kashmiri salted pink tea (noon chai) brewed with green tea leaves, milk, salt and a pinch of baking soda, served with girda — a soft, slightly crisp tandoori-style bread. The everyday Kashmiri breakfast.
ingredients: Green tea leaves, milk, salt, baking soda for noon chai
Flour, yeast or starter, salt for girda
steps: Brew strong green tea with baking soda until it turns pinkish; add milk and salt.
Prepare and bake or tandoor-cook girda bread.
Serve hot tea with fresh bread, sometimes with butter or local preserve.
tips: Noon chai is distinctly salty, not sweet; an acquired taste for many outsiders.

title: Harissa
description: Slow-cooked winter breakfast of minced mutton and rice pounded into a smooth, porridge-like consistency, seasoned with fennel and whole spices. Served hot at dawn, often with a drizzle of tempered fat.
ingredients: Mustard oil or mutton fat for finishing
steps: Slow-cook mutton and rice with spices for many hours, stirring and pounding until smooth.
Temper a little fat with shallots or chillies if desired.
Serve hot in small bowls.
tips: Traditionally cooked overnight by specialised harisa-guyrs; a true winter specialty.

title: Rogan Josh
description: Iconic Kashmiri lamb/mutton curry with a deep red colour from Kashmiri chillies (and traditionally ratan jot), fragrant with fennel, dry ginger and yogurt. A cornerstone of both Wazwan and home cooking.
ingredients: Yogurt, Kashmiri red chilli powder, fennel powder, dry ginger
Whole spices (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon), mustard oil or ghee
Shallots or hing (depending on Muslim or Pandit style)
steps: Brown meat in hot oil with whole spices.
Add yogurt and powdered spices; cook on low heat until meat is tender and gravy is rich and red.
Finish with a touch of saffron or ratan jot extract if available.
Serve with steamed rice.
tips: Authentic versions are aromatic rather than extremely spicy; colour comes from mild Kashmiri chillies.

title: Yakhni
description: Mild, pale yogurt-based mutton curry flavoured with green cardamom, fennel and dry ginger. The gentle counterpart to the richer red curries of Kashmir; a Wazwan and everyday staple.
ingredients: Thick yogurt, fennel powder, dry ginger, green cardamom, cloves
steps: Cook mutton with whole spices until tender.
Whisk yogurt and incorporate slowly into the pot on low heat, stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
Simmer until the gravy is smooth and aromatic.
Serve with rice.
tips: Keep the heat low when adding yogurt to maintain a silky texture.

title: Haak (Collard Greens)
description: Simple yet essential Kashmiri preparation of collard greens (haak) cooked in mustard oil with asafoetida, whole red chillies and minimal spices. A daily vegetable in both Pandit and Muslim homes.
ingredients: Mustard oil, hing (asafoetida), whole dried red chillies
steps: Clean and roughly chop the greens.
Heat mustard oil, add hing and whole chillies.
Add haak and a little water; cook covered until tender but still vibrant.
Serve with rice.
tips: Often cooked with radish (haak-muji) or lotus stem for variation.

title: Kashmiri Dum Aloo
description: Whole baby potatoes pricked, fried and slow-cooked in a yogurt-based gravy flavoured with fennel, dry ginger and Kashmiri chilli. A classic vegetarian dish of the Valley, quite different from the spicier Punjabi version.
ingredients: Yogurt, Kashmiri chilli powder, fennel powder, dry ginger
Whole spices, mustard oil or ghee
steps: Fry the pricked potatoes until lightly golden.
Prepare a yogurt-spice gravy.
Add potatoes and simmer on low heat (dum) until the gravy is absorbed and thickened.
Serve with rice or bread.
tips: Pricking the potatoes allows the gravy to penetrate deeply.

title: Gushtaba
description: Large, velvety mutton meatballs made from finely pounded meat, simmered in a rich yogurt gravy. Traditionally the final, ceremonial dish of a Wazwan feast — the ‘dish of kings’.
ingredients: Yogurt, milk or cream, fennel, cardamom, salt
steps: Pound the meat until very smooth and aerated; form large balls.
Prepare a yogurt-based gravy with whole spices.
Gently simmer the meatballs until cooked through and the gravy is silky.
Serve as the concluding course with rice.
tips: The texture of the meatball depends on thorough pounding; traditionally done with a wooden mallet.

title: Rista
description: Smaller mutton meatballs cooked in a rich red gravy coloured with Kashmiri chilli. One of the essential courses of the traditional Wazwan.
ingredients: Kashmiri chilli, yogurt or stock, spices
Onion/shallot base or hing depending on tradition
steps: Form small meatballs from well-minced meat.
Prepare a red gravy with chilli and spices.
Simmer the meatballs gently until cooked and the gravy is glossy.
Serve with rice as part of a multi-course meal.
tips: Rista is typically redder and spicier than the white gushtaba.

title: Tabak Maaz
description: Lamb ribs boiled in spiced milk or water then fried in ghee until crisp and golden. A prized starter or early course in Wazwan, known for its rich fat and crisp exterior.
ingredients: Milk or water, salt, garlic or spices for boiling
steps: Boil the ribs with salt and mild aromatics until tender.
Drain and fry in hot ghee until the exterior is crisp and lacquered.
Serve hot as an appetiser or early course.
tips: The contrast of crisp exterior and soft, fatty meat is the hallmark.

title: Nadru Yakhni
description: Lotus stem (nadru) cooked in a delicate yogurt gravy with fennel, cardamom and dry ginger. A refined vegetarian dish that mirrors the technique of mutton yakhni.
ingredients: Yogurt, fennel powder, dry ginger, green cardamom
steps: Clean and slice lotus stem; boil briefly if needed.
Prepare a yogurt-based gravy with whole and powdered spices.
Add the lotus stem and simmer until tender and the gravy is smooth.
Serve with rice.
tips: Lotus stem should retain a slight crunch.

title: Nadru Monje
description: Crispy deep-fried fritters of lotus stem coated in a spiced rice-flour or gram-flour batter. A popular Kashmiri tea-time and appetiser snack.
ingredients: Rice flour or besan, chilli powder, salt, spices
steps: Slice lotus stem thinly and marinate lightly.
Coat in spiced batter.
Deep-fry until golden and crisp.
Serve hot with chutney.
tips: Best eaten immediately while still crisp.

title: Kashmiri Seekh Kebab
description: Minced lamb mixed with Kashmiri spices including cardamom, black cumin, saffron and Kashmiri chilli, moulded onto skewers and grilled over charcoal. A classic Wazwan starter and popular snack across the Valley.
ingredients: Cardamom powder, black cumin seeds, saffron, coriander, Kashmiri chilli, turmeric
Eggs for binding, oil for grilling
steps: Mix minced meat thoroughly with spices and eggs.
Shape onto skewers.
Grill over charcoal until cooked and lightly charred.
Serve with mint chutney and onion.
tips: Eggs help the kebab hold its shape around the skewer; a light hand with spices keeps the Kashmiri character.

title: Chaman Pakora
description: Cottage cheese (chaman/paneer) cubes marinated in a special Kashmiri spice paste and deep-fried. A traditional Kashmiri Pandit snack, often served as an appetiser or tea-time item.
ingredients: Besan or rice flour for coating (optional), oil
steps: Marinate paneer in spices.
Coat lightly if desired and deep-fry or shallow-fry until golden.
Serve hot with chutney.
tips: Can also be finished in a tomato or yogurt gravy as a main.
